evidence.claim: CMS said up to 720,000 pregnant and postpartum people could receive 12 months of Medicaid or CHIP coverage after pregnancy under the American Rescue Plan option.
evidence.title: Thousands More People with Medicaid and CHIP Coverage Now Eligible to Access Critical Postpartum Coverage Thanks to the American Rescue Plan
evidence.excerpt: CMS said up to 720,000 pregnant and postpartum people could receive 12 months of Medicaid or CHIP coverage after pregnancy under the American Rescue Plan option.
evidence.source_locator: first two paragraphs of the CMS release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary coverage-policy announcement with a concrete beneficiary estimate and direct public-health rationale.
evidence.period_fit: Exactly in-period and directly about maternal coverage in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Biden's administration through ARP implementation and CMS action, though states had to opt in.
contrary_evidence: The policy depended on state uptake, so realized coverage was uneven.

evidence.claim: Biden directed HHS to consider actions to expand access to reproductive healthcare, including travel across state lines where permitted, and to improve data collection on maternal and reproductive health outcomes.
evidence.title: Executive Order 14079 - Securing Access to Reproductive and Other Healthcare Services
evidence.excerpt: Biden directed HHS to consider actions to expand access to reproductive healthcare, including travel across state lines where permitted, and to improve data collection on maternal and reproductive health outcomes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential legal text with direct ruler attribution and concrete administrative directions.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 after Dobbs and squarely within the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action by Biden, implemented through executive authority over the federal branch.
contrary_evidence: The order is limited by federal law and does not itself guarantee access in restrictive states.

evidence.claim: CMS said the Inflation Reduction Act would lower Medicare drug costs, cap insulin co-pays at $35 per month, limit Medicare Part D out-of-pocket costs, and extend enhanced ACA tax credits for three years.
evidence.title: Statements by CMS Leadership on President Biden Signing Inflation Reduction Act into Law
evidence.excerpt: CMS said the Inflation Reduction Act would lower Medicare drug costs, cap insulin co-pays at $35 per month, limit Medicare Part D out-of-pocket costs, and extend enhanced ACA tax credits for three years.
evidence.source_locator: statement paragraphs on Medicare and Marketplace savings
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary CMS response to a newly enacted law, with specific household-cost provisions and direct implementation relevance.
evidence.period_fit: In-period and tied to a major 2022 social-welfare law.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Biden because he signed the law and his administration framed and implemented it, though Congress shaped the final statute.
contrary_evidence: The biggest savings were prospective and would phase in over time, not all realized immediately in 2022.

evidence.claim: CMS finalized rules that made Medicare coverage start the month after enrollment, expanded special enrollment periods, and reduced gaps and late-enrollment penalties for eligible beneficiaries.
evidence.title: Biden-Harris Administration Strengthens Medicare with Finalized Policies to Simplify Enrollment and Expand Access to Coverage
evidence.excerpt: CMS finalized rules that made Medicare coverage start the month after enrollment, expanded special enrollment periods, and reduced gaps and late-enrollment penalties for eligible beneficiaries.
evidence.source_locator: press release summary on coverage timing and special enrollment
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary CMS policy announcement with concrete access changes for Medicare beneficiaries.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to access and administrative simplification.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Biden's administration through CMS rulemaking authority, not personal day-to-day control.
contrary_evidence: This is administrative improvement rather than a complete structural overhaul of Medicare.

evidence.claim: HUD announced a $322 million package plus $43 million for roughly 4,000 new Housing Choice Vouchers to connect homeless and vulnerable households to housing, health care, and supportive services.
evidence.title: Biden Administration Announces First-Ever Funding Opportunity for Coordinated Approaches to Address Unsheltered Homelessness, Including Resources for Rural Communities
evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
evidence.excerpt: HUD announced a $322 million package plus $43 million for roughly 4,000 new Housing Choice Vouchers to connect homeless and vulnerable households to housing, health care, and supportive services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary HUD release with exact dollar amounts and a direct service-delivery description.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and targeted at a major welfare and homelessness crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Biden's administration through HUD and ARP-linked housing policy, though local administration matters for actual take-up.
contrary_evidence: The package is a first step and does not by itself resolve homelessness nationally.

evidence.claim: HUD awarded more than 19,000 new Housing Choice Vouchers to nearly 2,000 public housing agencies, describing it as the most expansive allocation of flexible new rental assistance in 20 years and part of nearly 100,000 new vouchers supported by ARP and the FY 2022 budget.
evidence.title: FACT SHEET: HUD Awards More Than 19,000 New Housing Choice Vouchers in Most Expansive Allocation of Flexible Rental Assistance in 20 Years
evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
evidence.excerpt: HUD awarded more than 19,000 new Housing Choice Vouchers to nearly 2,000 public housing agencies, describing it as the most expansive allocation of flexible new rental assistance in 20 years and part of nearly 100,000 new vouchers supported by ARP and the FY 2022 budget.
evidence.source_locator: fact sheet opening paragraph and voucher allocation summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary HUD allocation announcement with precise counts and a clear link to vulnerable-household support.
evidence.period_fit: In-period and directly about housing access in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Biden's administration and budget choices, while local agencies and states controlled delivery.
contrary_evidence: Voucher allocation is helpful but does not prove that housing outcomes improved uniformly by year-end 2022.

evidence.claim: USDA said it would provide nearly $1 billion in additional funding to schools for purchasing American-grown foods and would keep supporting direct certification and other school-meal flexibilities for higher-need children.
evidence.title: Biden Administration Takes Additional Steps to Strengthen Child Nutrition Programs
evidence.excerpt: USDA said it would provide nearly $1 billion in additional funding to schools for purchasing American-grown foods and would keep supporting direct certification and other school-meal flexibilities for higher-need children.
evidence.source_locator: press release body and bullet list of flexibilities
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary USDA release with concrete funding and implementation details for child nutrition.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to child nutrition and school access.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Biden through USDA leadership and federal nutrition authority, though school districts implement the programs.
contrary_evidence: The release itself says this does not restore universal free meals for all students in 2022-23.

evidence.claim: USDA said the September 2022 White House Conference would focus on nutrition security, that tens of millions of Americans face food insecurity and diet-related disease, and that USDA was updating WIC and school-meal policies as part of that effort.
evidence.title: White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health - It is almost here!
evidence.excerpt: USDA said the September 2022 White House Conference would focus on nutrition security, that tens of millions of Americans face food insecurity and diet-related disease, and that USDA was updating WIC and school-meal policies as part of that effort.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs describing the conference and ongoing FNS actions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary USDA pre-conference statement with clear policy framing and in-period timing.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and about the administration's nutrition agenda.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Biden's administration through White House and USDA policy direction.
contrary_evidence: The page is an announcement and policy framing, not evidence of completed nationwide outcomes.

evidence.claim: FDA issued guidance to temporarily exercise enforcement discretion for certain infant-formula requirements in order to increase infant formula supplies in the United States while still checking safety and nutritional adequacy.
evidence.title: FDA to Provide Flexibility to Manufacturers to Increase Infant Formula Supplies
evidence.excerpt: FDA issued guidance to temporarily exercise enforcement discretion for certain infant-formula requirements in order to increase infant formula supplies in the United States while still checking safety and nutritional adequacy.
evidence.source_locator: original constituent update and guidance summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary regulatory guidance directly responding to a public-health and supply crisis.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to a major infant-nutrition emergency.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Biden's administration through FDA/HHS crisis management, not to personal direct control of every operational detail.
contrary_evidence: Enforcement discretion is a crisis workaround, not a durable fix for infant-formula market fragility.

evidence.claim: Biden announced a three-part student-debt plan that would cancel $10,000 for eligible borrowers, up to $20,000 for Pell Grant recipients, and target relief toward lower- and middle-income borrowers.
evidence.title: FACT SHEET: President Biden Announces Student Loan Relief for Borrowers Who Need It Most
evidence.excerpt: Biden announced a three-part student-debt plan that would cancel $10,000 for eligible borrowers, up to $20,000 for Pell Grant recipients, and target relief toward lower- and middle-income borrowers.
evidence.source_locator: fact sheet summary paragraphs at the top of the document
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential fact sheet with concrete benefit design and income targeting.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to education access and household burden.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential initiative by Biden, though implementation depended on legal and administrative follow-through.
contrary_evidence: The policy was later challenged and partly blocked, so 2022 announcement and realized impact are not identical.

evidence.claim: The Education Department said it would discharge remaining federal student loans for about 208,000 borrowers who attended ITT Technical Institute, totaling $3.9 billion, and would begin recouping approved claims from DeVry University.
evidence.title: White House Press Release - Education Department Approves $3.9 Billion Group Discharge for 208,000 Borrowers Who Attended ITT Technical Institute
evidence.excerpt: The Education Department said it would discharge remaining federal student loans for about 208,000 borrowers who attended ITT Technical Institute, totaling $3.9 billion, and would begin recouping approved claims from DeVry University.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary federal relief announcement with a specific borrower count and dollar amount.
evidence.period_fit: In-period and directly relevant to correcting a harmful education-market failure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Biden's Education Department leadership and his broader student-loan agenda.
contrary_evidence: Targeted borrower relief addresses past wrongdoing; it does not by itself reform the entire higher-education market.

evidence.claim: FDA said it was temporarily exercising enforcement discretion to increase infant-formula supply in the United States, while still asking manufacturers to show safety and nutritional adequacy.
evidence.title: Guidance for Industry: Infant Formula Enforcement Discretion Policy
evidence.excerpt: FDA said it was temporarily exercising enforcement discretion to increase infant-formula supply in the United States, while still asking manufacturers to show safety and nutritional adequacy.
evidence.source_locator: opening guidance summary and purpose section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary regulatory guidance from the agency handling the shortage; clear crisis-response document.
evidence.period_fit: In-period and directly tied to the 2022 formula shortage.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Biden's administration through FDA/HHS crisis management and delegated authority.
contrary_evidence: This is an emergency supply measure, not proof that the broader infant-formula market became stable in 2022.

evidence.claim: Census reported that the official poverty rate in 2022 was 11.5 percent and the Supplemental Poverty Measure rose to 12.4 percent because temporary Child Tax Credit, EITC, and stimulus expansions expired.
evidence.title: Income, Poverty and Health Insurance Coverage in the United States: 2022
evidence.excerpt: Census reported that the official poverty rate in 2022 was 11.5 percent and the Supplemental Poverty Measure rose to 12.4 percent because temporary Child Tax Credit, EITC, and stimulus expansions expired.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary Census publication using standard national income and poverty measures; strong for household-welfare context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partly attributable to Biden because the deterioration reflected the end of temporary pandemic-relief policies plus inflation and distributional effects beyond direct presidential control.
contrary_evidence: The report also shows the official poverty measure was unchanged from 2021, so the picture is mixed rather than uniformly worsening.

evidence.claim: USDA said 12.8 percent of U.S. households were food insecure in 2022, up from 10.2 percent in 2021, and very low food security also increased.
evidence.title: Prevalence of U.S. household food insecurity increased in 2022
evidence.publisher: Economic Research Service, U.S. Department of Agriculture
evidence.excerpt: USDA said 12.8 percent of U.S. households were food insecure in 2022, up from 10.2 percent in 2021, and very low food security also increased.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary USDA/ERS annual food-security estimate, useful as a direct contrary indicator for household welfare.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 household conditions, though published later.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a national condition under Biden, but it reflects inflation, food prices, and household constraints as much as federal policy.
contrary_evidence: Food insecurity remained substantial despite major federal nutrition programs and health coverage gains.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 evidence on command-and-control or custody changes beyond declaratory policy and reactive crisis signaling.
Limited direct evidence on internal U.S.-Ukraine operational restrictions and private bargaining with Russia.
Weak direct evidence on federal prison/detention conditions and on whether the listed reforms materially reduced abuse in 2022.
Little direct evidence on electoral manipulation, subnational election protection outcomes, or media/platform pressure beyond speeches and DOJ initiatives.
Direct evidence on appointment quality and empowered economic professionals is thinner than the policy and macro-outcome record.
Outcome evidence is strong on access and targeted relief, but weaker on durable, independent measurement of household welfare change within 2022.
No direct 2022 forensic finding, ethics violation, or investigative record tying Joe Biden personally to self-dealing, concealment, or family benefit.
Appointment and patronage evidence around Biden's own circle remains thin.
Much of the evidence is still program-design and rollout architecture rather than completed, award-level implementation output.
